## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle struct at 68 B/particle gives loop 1 32 hot bytes (age+pos+seed+vel, 47%) and loop 2 28 hot bytes (color+pos, 41%) — the rest is dead weight in every cacheline fill. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers; respawn branches to a spawn call. Identity ordering yields sequential 68-byte strides for the prefetcher, but all measured working sets (N≥10000 → 680 KB) exceed L2 (512 KB); N≤100000 stays in L3 (16 MB), N≥1000000 spills to DRAM.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across N within each regime: at q=0.01, 24.5 ns/p at N=10000 rises to 26.2 at N=10M — 7% across the L3→DRAM transition. At q=0.5 it is even flatter (33.8→33.7). L1d spill (N≈481) and L2 spill (N≈7710) both fall below the smallest measured point. The absence of a steep knee at the L3→DRAM boundary (N≈246723) signals the algo is not memory-bound — cost is governed by per-particle instruction count, not by cache residency.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.0–2.8 GB/s against the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 16–22% of peak. The memory floor (5.359 ns/p) means the algo runs at 4.5–6.3× the irreducible memory time. The profile confirms frontend-bound: frontend_stall 62–70%, backend 0%, branch_flush 0%. Against the scalar baseline it is 0.96–0.99× — no auto-vec benefit. Against the winner (LP2-opt) it is 1.76–3.24× slower, narrowing at high death rates (3.24× at q=0.01 vs 1.76× at q=0.5) because respawn compute dominates and the winner's render advantage shrinks proportionally.

## Assembly
Vector-suffixed instructions = 0: no auto-vectorization across particles. The 345-instruction body uses scalar SSE — vmovss (17), vmulss (5), vucomiss (11) — one particle per iteration at 0x44 stride. vmulps/vaddps (3 each) parallelize only 3-component pos/vel math within a single particle. Death is branchy (vucomiss + jae + jne), respawn calls spawn. The render loop does byte-granular scatter — movzx BYTE PTR, add, cmp, cmovae, mov BYTE PTR — per R/G/B channel. This instruction volume explains the 62–70% frontend stalls: decode cannot feed enough μops to saturate memory or compute.

## Verdict
Refuted — zero vector-suffixed instructions and 0.96–0.99× of the scalar baseline at every point: auto-vectorization provided no benefit. The algo is 1.76–3.24× slower than the winner, achieving 16–22% of ceiling. The mechanism is a 345-instruction scalar loop — branchy per-particle death/respawn plus byte-granular render scatter — that bottlenecks on frontend decode (62–70% frontend stalls), never reaching the bandwidth wall where the 47% hot-byte fraction would matter.
